[2025-03-31] standup/boreal/2025-03-31-2: We agreed today that the notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff. The reason is that the flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages.

1. "We agreed today that the notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff." - This is a decision about the notifier's retry behavior. Durable fact/decision.

2. "The reason is that the flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages." - This explains the reason. It also implies the previous behavior was a flat one-second retry. This is context/reasoning. Should I capture this? It's durable background info: the previous retry policy was a flat one-second retry. Hmm, but is that a "durable fact"? It could be. The decision is the main fact. The reason could be part of the decision's evidence or a separate fact. I think the main fact is the decision. Possibly add a fact about the reason: "The notifier's previous flat one-second retry hammered the push provider during its outages." That's a durable statement about why. But do we want to include "push provider" as an entity? It's mentioned. Entities: notifier, push provider.

The instructions: "Do not invent anything the note does not say." The reason is stated in the note, so it's fine to include. But is it durable? It's a rationale. I could include it as part of the decision fact's evidence. I think one fact (the decision) plus possibly one relation? No relationship between two entities stated—well, notifier retries pushes to push provider? Not really a relation of the given kinds. The decision is about notifier.

Also note mentions "We" = Boreal team presumably (standup/boreal). The decision is made by Boreal? Could add relation Boreal maintains notifier already exists (memory 1000061: Boreal owns notifier). No new relation needed.

So output:

  {
   "content": "The notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff.",
   "entities": ["notifier"],
   "kind": "decision",
   "confidence": 0.95,
   "evidence": "the notifier will retry failed pushes three times with exponential backoff"
  },
  {
   "content": "The notifier's earlier flat one-second retry hammered the push provider during its outages.",
   "entities": ["notifier", "push provider"],
   "kind": "fact",
   "confidence": 0.9,
   "evidence": "the flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during its outages"
  }
 ]
}

Should the second fact be included? It's context about the reason. It is durable in the sense that it explains why. I think including it is reasonable, but maybe risky—it's more of a rationale. The instructions say list new durable facts the note states. The note states this as a reason. I'd include it as a fact since it documents why the change was made, useful later. Alternatively, keep it simpler with only the decision. I'll include both; the reason is a factual statement.

Actually, careful: "was hammering" - past behavior. The new content: "The notifier's previous flat one-second retry was hammering the push provider during outages." That's fine.

No corrections, no relations, no aliases.

Should confidence be included? Optional fields. I'll include kind and confidence.
